notes.title: 0.52 Major Content Update
notes.content: [p]Hello everyone,[/p][p]Thank you so much for your patience—this update turned out far bigger than we first expected, and we’re really excited to finally share it with you! Our main goal with this update is to make Coreless’s battles feel sharper, more dynamic, and more rewarding, while simplifying systems that previously cluttered the moment-to-moment experience.[/p][p] [/p][h3][b]1. Map Progression[/b][/h3][p]The progression system has been fully revamped. Coreless now features shorter, mission-based gameplay tied together with a structured map. Completing each mission node unlocks tougher challenges, along with new powers and characters. Missions have also been redesigned to feel more engaging and focused.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]2. Session Progression[/b][/h3][p]The session experience has been overhauled to put more focus on slaying monsters and building your run. You now gain experience by defeating enemies, completing objectives, and taking on challenge events. Each time you level up, you can select from a range of upgrades, powers, and mods to enhance your character for that run.[/p][p]The overall flow now leans closer to a Survivor-like experience, while still built around Coreless’s battle system. You can equip up to two powers per run, and consumables have been removed. All powers and abilities are now significantly more impactful, giving you the freedom to choose which ones to invest in as you shape your build.[/p][p]Overdrive Abilities no longer require charging by default, but with the right upgrades you can enable charge mechanics for massively amplified effects. Your movement is also less restricted when charging Overdrive abilities. The design space left behind by the removal of consumables will be further explored in future updates.[/p][p] [/p][h3][b]3. Research System[/b][/h3][p]A brand-new Research System has been added alongside the Talent Tree, giving you more ways to strengthen your characters and powers. Spend Printed Circuit to specialize in your favorite abilities or characters, unlocking permanent perks, upgrades, and stat boosts. As you unlock more Powers and Characters, more Research options open up.[/p][p] [/p][h3][b]4. Shop System & Addon Update[/b][/h3][p]The old Tick System for addons has been replaced by a new Shop System, making it clearer and more flexible to choose what you want. The shop refreshes its inventory as you play, offering a wider selection. Addons have also been rebalanced to be much stronger, and many now include in-session upgrades—allowing you to craft builds that lean heavily on addons as well as powers.[/p][p] [/p][h3][b]5. Talent Tree Update[/b][/h3][p]The Talent Tree has been streamlined: stats are stronger, and redundant nodes have been removed so every choice feels more impactful.[/p][p] [/p][h3][b]6. Resources & Profile Rating Update[/b][/h3][p]Printed Circuit is now the universal currency for all meta-progression. Profile Rating no longer depends on Mech Debris and instead levels up through its own experience system. Complete sessions to raise your profile level, while Printed Circuit fuels Research, Addons, and other upgrades.[/p][p] [/p][h3][b]7. Removed Features[/b][/h3][p]We’ve removed several systems that we felt added more clutter and confusion than meaningful fun. This includes Ticks, Consumables, and Cyphers. While we still like the original ideas behind these features, their current implementations weren’t effective. We’ll look for better ways to reintroduce these elements in the future.[/p][p] [/p][p][/p][p]This is only the surface, there are plenty more changes waiting to be discovered, so take your time exploring and let us know what you think![/p][p][/p][p]Your previous progress (profile rating, addons, and character unlocks) is preserved. That said, we recommend starting a fresh save to fully experience the new systems from the beginning. [b]If you stick with your old save, you’ll still need to replay from the first mission to unlock all the powers and progression content.[/b][/p][p] [/p][p]You may also notice that the new character isn’t included yet. With this update being such a major overhaul, we want to make sure the systems settle in smoothly before adding more complexity. The character update is planned for next month, and we’ll share more details as we get closer.[/p][p] [/p][p]Thanks again for playing and supporting us! This is our biggest step forward yet, and we can’t wait to hear your feedback![/p][p] [/p][p]All the best,[/p][p]Turtles[/p]

tags.feature: The progression system has been fully revamped. Coreless now features shorter, mission-based gameplay tied together with a structured map. Completing each mission node unlocks tougher challenges, along with new powers and characters. Missions have also been redesigned to feel more engaging and focused.

The session experience has been overhauled to put more focus on slaying monsters and building your run. You now gain experience by defeating enemies, completing objectives, and taking on challenge events. Each time you level up, you can select from a range of upgrades, powers, and mods to enhance your character for that run.

You can equip up to two powers per run, and consumables have been removed. All powers and abilities are now significantly more impactful, giving you the freedom to choose which ones to invest in as you shape your build.

Overdrive Abilities no longer require charging by default, but with the right upgrades you can enable charge mechanics for massively amplified effects. Your movement is also less restricted when charging Overdrive abilities. The design space left behind by the removal of consumables will be further explored in future updates.

A brand-new Research System has been added alongside the Talent Tree, giving you more ways to strengthen your characters and powers. Spend Printed Circuit to specialize in your favorite abilities or characters, unlocking permanent perks, upgrades, and stat boosts. As you unlock more Powers and Characters, more Research options open up.

The old Tick System for addons has been replaced by a new Shop System, making it clearer and more flexible to choose what you want. The shop refreshes its inventory as you play, offering a wider selection. Addons have also been rebalanced to be much stronger, and many now include in-session upgrades—allowing you to craft builds that lean heavily on addons as well as powers.
The Talent Tree has been streamlined: stats are stronger, and redundant nodes have been removed so every choice feels more impactful.

Printed Circuit is now the universal currency for all meta-progression. Profile Rating no longer depends on Mech Debris and instead levels up through its own experience system. Complete sessions to raise your profile level, while Printed Circuit fuels Research, Addons, and other upgrades.

We’ve removed several systems that we felt added more clutter and confusion than meaningful fun. This includes Ticks, Consumables, and Cyphers. While we still like the original ideas behind these features, their current implementations weren’t effective. We’ll look for better ways to reintroduce these elements in the future.

notes.title: Devlog 1 – Upcoming Major Update Preview
notes.content:
[p]Hey all, happy weekend![/p][p]Just a quick update on what we’re working on and the thought process behind some of the major upcoming system changes.[/p][p]From the initial launch feedback, we’ve identified two main takeaways:[/p][olist][*][p][b]Confusion around game mechanics and a lack of progressive onboarding.[/b]
The current structure feels a bit chaotic — key systems like Mechanical Cores, Overdrive, Consumables, and Cyphers are all introduced at once, without a smooth ramp-up. This results in several issues: gameplay can feel unforgiving, core mechanics may be unclear, and the pacing of content, addons, and unlockables feels uneven. [/p][/*][*][p][b]Strong, engaging moment-to-moment gameplay once players “click” with the mechanics.[/b]
When players push past the early confusion and start using key systems as intended, or when the game loop naturally flows for them, the experience becomes very fun and rewarding.[/p][/*][/olist][p]On the first point — we don’t think a simple tutorial will solve the problem. The mechanics are already dense enough that adding more explanation could make early gameplay tedious, hurt the sense of progression, and add friction to onboarding. More importantly, the extra complexity might not be worth the trade-off. The good news is that, once the friction is reduced, the core game loop is already strong enough to stand on its own without relying on so many extra mechanics to create moment-to-moment engagement.[/p][p]Sorry if this sounds overly “academic” >< — what we really mean is: the core loop is fun and complex enough without piling on things like:[/p][list][*][p]Scarce health recovery[/p][/*][*][p]Mechanical Cores as a fourth resource to manage[/p][/*][*][p]Too many powers to swap between in a single run[/p][/*][/list][p]Our goal is to tighten up all mechanics so they better serve the engaging parts of the game, reduce noise, and pace optional systems so they appear later, rather than all at once at the start. [/p][p][/p][h2][b]So, what’s changing in the upcoming major update[/b][/h2][list][*][p]A [b]new progression system[/b] will replace the current difficulty tier system. It’s a map-like structure where each node represents a step forward.[/p][list][*][p][b]Normal nodes[/b]: 1 stage, completable in about 20 minutes.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Challenge nodes[/b]: 2+ stages, requiring more planning.[/p][/*][*][p]Some nodes will contain unlockables or unique addon drops.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Refined upgrades and powers[/b]: Powers will be more impactful, easier to use, and won’t require constant swapping.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Mechanical Cores removed[/b]: The Energy system will be reworked into a generation/spender model for both normal and Overdrive abilities, making resource management more fluid. Some builds will allow instant Overdrive casting.[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44638370/afe23613ea9c18403414b0c38d411e35a2567727.png"][/img][/p][p]Overall, we want sessions to feel more engaging, less restrictive, and occasionally even overpowered — while still retaining a good layer of tactical decision-making.[/p][p]These are big changes, and we expect to refine them further after the update once we see how they play in practice.[/p][p]Oh, and yes — a [b]new character[/b] is in development! We’ll share more on that later.[/p][p]The patch is planned for later this month. Everything mentioned here is still subject to change as development continues.[/p][p]Thanks for reading all the way to the end — you’re the best!
Talk to you soon.[/p][p]— BlueTurtle[/p]

tags.feature: A [b]new progression system[/b] will replace the current difficulty tier system. It’s a map-like structure where each node represents a step forward.
Normal nodes: 1 stage, completable in about 20 minutes.
Challenge nodes: 2+ stages, requiring more planning.
Some nodes will contain unlockables or unique addon drops.
Refined upgrades and powers: Powers will be more impactful, easier to use, and won’t require constant swapping.

Mechanical Cores removed: The Energy system will be reworked into a generation/spender model for both normal and Overdrive abilities, making resource management more fluid. Some builds will allow instant Overdrive casting.
Oh, and yes — a [b]new character[/b] is in development! We’ll share more on that later.

notes.title: A Patch, a Thank-You, and Devlog 0
notes.content: [h1]Thank You[/h1][p]Hey everyone,[/p][p]Thank you all for joining us in this very early stage of Coreless's development. Your support during the first week has been incredibly heartwarming and encouraging.[/p][p]Coreless launched in a minimal but functional state — something closer to the old-school spirit of Early Access. As a small team,  this approach allows us to stay nimble, avoid building in a vacuum, and grow the game with players, not ahead of them.[/p][p]Of course, this approach comes with risks, especially in today’s competitive landscape where most EA titles are polished and well-funded. That’s why we’re deeply grateful to everyone who chose to dive in despite the game’s rough edges — your early support truly means the world to us.[/p][p]We’re committed to making Coreless the best version of itself. Not just because of your backing, but because there’s a lot we want to express through this game.[/p][p][/p][p]Coreless gives us a flexible foundation to explore a variety of exciting design directions, such as:[/p][p]— Enhancing fast-paced tactical combat  [/p][p]— Embracing a more classic, unforgiving roguelike structure  [/p][p]— Adopting survivor-like, upgrade-driven systems  [/p][p]— Experimenting with strategic planning and resource management[/p][p]Coreless already shows promise in how expressive its systems can be — even in this early state. With your feedback, we can shape it into something truly special.[/p][p]Gameplay mechanics are our strength, and we work hard — so let’s get started. :)[/p][p][/p][h1]Patch Notes [/h1][p]Along with this first thank-you letter, we're also releasing our first patch, focused primarily on onboarding improvements and game flow clarity. Here’s what’s included:[/p][olist][*][p][b]New Difficulty Setting (now renamed to "Sequence")[/b][/p][p]A new introductory sequence has been added with basic tutorial guidance.[/p][/*][*][p][b]UI Clarity Improvements[/b][/p][p]Several UI elements have been updated to better communicate mechanics like the Poise Meter, Potential Rewards, etc. More improvements are coming in future patches.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Stage 1 & 2 Improvement[/b][/p][p]These stages now follow a timeline system, spawning elite packs at set intervals. Defeating them grants upgrade rewards. This improves flow clarity and allows players to plan their exploration.[/p][p]Also, shrines in Stage 1 now require manual activation, giving players more control over when to begin challenges. [b]Let us know how this change feels — it’s a substantial shift in early-stage exploration.[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Difficulty Renamed to “Sequence”[/b][/p][p]Formerly Easy/Normal/Hard, the system is now CX-0, CX-1, CX-2, etc. This sets the stage for a major content update next month.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Monster Balancing[/b][/p][p]Overall monster difficulty has been reduced to improve pacing and approachability. Stage 4 still needs more work, and we'll be releasing patches in coming weeks for it.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Power & Path Upgrades Rebalanced[/b][/p][p]Powers are now easier to obtain and fill out, while Path upgrades appear less frequently. Further tuning for Path upgrades is planned.[/p][/*][*][p][b]New Unique Addon: “Maintainer’s Toolkit”[/b][/p][p]This addon is now granted once when the player first starts the game. It’s designed to provide early stability and subtly reflects the current state of the Coreless world.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Boss Spawns No Longer Remove Interactables[/b][/p][p]All interactables now remain active even when a boss appears.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Kat's Overdrive Targeting Toggle[/b][/p][p]You can now toggle Kat's Overdrive to prioritize elites and bosses.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Booster Upgrades Rebalanced[/b][/p][p]Crit Booster has been removed; Attack Speed Booster is now more effective. A new booster that increases Overdrive Haste has been added. Overdrive positioning in the game will receive further tweaks in future updates.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Expanded Reward Pool[/b][/p][p]Many more consumables can now drop as rewards.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Miscellaneous Fixes[/b][/p][p]Various bug fixes and general improvements.[/p][/*][/olist][h1]Upcoming Major Content Update[/h1][p]We’ll likely continue releasing small hotfixes to address any urgent issues as they come up. Meanwhile, we’re working on our [b]first major content update[/b], [b]scheduled for next month.[/b] We’ll share more information as we get closer — stay tuned.[/p][p]Thanks again — and we wish you all a wonderful weekend![/p][p]— Blue Turtle[/p]

notes.content:
[p]Thanks to everyone who’s picked up [b]Coreless[/b] and taken the time to share your thoughts so far.[/p][p]This is our first patch, addressing critical bugs and smoothing out some of the roughest edges. We're also working on improving how the game’s systems are introduced — you’ll see more of that in future updates.[/p][p]If you’ve had a chance to try [b]Coreless[/b], feel free to share your impressions — what’s working, what’s confusing, or what you’d like to see improved. Even a short Steam review/thread helps us understand how the game’s design is landing, and where to focus next.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Patch Notes:[/b][/p][p]1.      [b]Left Mouse Button[/b] is now dedicated to [b]Normal Strike[/b] only — you can hold the key to continuously perform normal strikes.[/p][p]2.      [b]Right Mouse Button[/b] is now assigned to [b]Overdrive Strike[/b] — hold to charge and release it.[/p][p]3.      Slightly reduced monster density during [b]Surge Events[/b].[/p][p]4.      [b]Shield mechanic updated[/b]:
If you take damage exceeding your shield value, the leftover damage will now be reduced by 30% instead of being fully blocked.[/p][p][i](This change aims to keep shield builds strategically rewarding while better balancing them with other defensive tools.)[/i][/p][p]5.      Increased the chance to drop consumables when elites are not [b]Terminated[/b].[/p][p]6.      Improved [b]Metal Gunner’s Weakpoint[/b] mechanic: now deals double damage and guarantees a critical strike.[/p][p]7.      Fixed an issue where [b]effect sounds[/b] were not properly linked to audio controls.[/p][p]8.      Added [b]Streamer Mode[/b], which disables background music to help avoid false copyright flags in recorded content.[/p][p]9.      Added [b]Inverted Y-axis[/b] option.[/p]

notes.title: Coreless Dev Update: Overdrive Abilities, Meta-Progression, and More!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

It’s been a while since our last update, and we’re excited to share some of the progress we’ve made on Coreless as we gear up for its Early Access launch later this year.

[h2]Improving the Moment-to-Moment Gameplay[/h2]

We were pretty happy with the overall session experience in our latest version, but something felt off. The pacing wasn’t quite right, and the gameplay lacked that extra push to keep things intense. So, we went back to the drawing board and are currently revamping the ability system.

[h2]Introducing Overdrive Abilities[/h2]

Overdrive abilities require holding down keys for a period of time before releasing them, and many can be charged through multiple stages to amplify their impact. They consume Energy and pack a much bigger punch than standard abilities, adding a tactical layer with a risk/reward tradeoff. This should create more engaging combat, encouraging players to make split-second decisions that could turn the tide of battle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44638370/685b6c97dfd130e0256b0ba898eb540c48581238.gif[/img]

[h2]Revamping the In-Session Upgrade System[/h2]

Stat stacking is fun—don’t worry, that’s still here—but we wanted to encourage more thoughtful decision-making instead of just chasing raw numbers. The new system introduces more diverse upgrade paths, making each run feel unique. We’ll dive deeper into in-session exploration changes in a future post!

[h2]Meta-Progression Updates: Talent Tree & Power Systems[/h2]

Meta-progression is where we want Coreless to shine, and we’ve made some big changes:

[list]
[*] More Meaningful Talent Tree Choices – We reworked the Talent Tree to ensure each decision feels impactful, rather than just incremental stat bumps.
[*] The Addon System – A new mechanic where Addons drop during adventures, granting powerful bonuses and random affixes. These can be socketed into the Talent Tree, allowing for deep build customization.
[*] Consumables Overhaul – Consumables now provide more strategic advantages, from basic health potions to immunity-based elixirs that could save you in a pinch.
[*] Affix System – Both Addons and Consumables now roll with affixes that further shape their impact, opening up even more ways to tweak and optimize your build.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44638370/9fe91bc519a89072f9d7ff5f296d260012cbbe9a.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44638370/a84cf9d28deed062f8c7df4a77fc2e4c9941dd94.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44638370/dff67bfcff26ac8a98ad573d6f0f40a07ffd3990.png[/img]

For example, the Addon Metallic Blitz allows you to throw a metallic bomb at a nearby target, dealing damage to both the target and surrounding units. If socketed into a 'Double-dash trigger' node, the bomb will be thrown whenever you double-dash. Alternatively, if placed in a 'Pickup trigger' node, the bomb will activate whenever you collect buffs, adding a layer of adaptability to your build.

Our ultimate vision for meta-progression in Coreless is to provide a space where players can make long-term and experimental decisions, refining their build in a gradual and strategic way. Meanwhile, the in-session experience should feel spontaneous, immediate, fun, and impactful.

[h2]Companions Are Now More Than Just Sidekicks[/h2]

Previously, Companions were a nice addition, but we felt they lacked depth. Now, each Companion comes with a dedicated set of abilities and passives, giving them a much larger role in your pre-session build. Your choice of Companion will significantly impact both your starting abilities and the upgrade options available during a run.

For example, Kat could equip Voltbringer to gain Energy Burst and Thunderbolt Sphere, enabling a melee-ranged hybrid build. Alternatively, she could go with Venom Weaver, gaining passive plague capabilities and the Overdrive ability Plague Blast, which detonates all nearby Plague effects for devastating area damage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44638370/c99b803af9ee215c96052a84e91386ffe8521c35.png[/img]

[h2]More to Come![/h2]

These are just some of the big changes coming to Coreless, and we’ve got plenty more in the works. We’ll be sharing more details over the coming months, so stay tuned!

Thanks for following our journey—we can’t wait for you to jump into Coreless!
